title: Generalized relations between arithmetic functions
summary: The aim of this article is to present in a self-contained way identities arising in elementary number theory, among which the following one: $$ \sum_{d\mid n}\frac{μ^2(d)}{\varphi(d)\,d^s}=\prod_{p\mid n}\left(1+\frac{1}{(p-1)p^s}\right). $$ This formula expresses a non-trivial divisor sum involving the Möbius function $μ$ and Euler's totient function $\varphi$ as a simple and explicit multiplicative expression. This is a generalization of the remarkable Dineva formula, which corresponds to $s=0$ and gives $n/\varphi(n)$ on the right-hand side. We explain why only squarefree divisors are…
